requested_parts: Speed of ordinary Repeat after Power made Slow
answers.answer: An ordinary Repeat uses the Power’s most recently assigned speed, so it repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately uses that explicit timing, directly after the originating use.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

requested_parts: Whether Powers/Special Rules measure Range through Ocean in play
Whether this makes all outside edges Coastal
answers.answer: Yes. With Ocean In Play, Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through Ocean as a land. Only lands touching printed Ocean are Coastal; other outer edges are cliffs.

evidence.text: - **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). answers.answer: No. One Damage does not destroy a healthy Town or City, whose Health is 2/3. Damage boosts add total Damage at that step and remain part of the original Power when determining what it destroyed, so boosted Damage can contribute to Mists of Oblivion’s destruction-based Fear.
